(303775) 2005 QU
182
(
provisional designation
2005 QU
182
) is a
trans-Neptunian object
in the
scattered disk
, estimated to be around 440 to 740 kilometres (270 to 460 miles) in diameter. It was discovered on 30 August 2005 by American astronomers
Mike Brown
,
David Rabinowitz
and
Chad Trujillo
at the
Palomar Observatory
in California.
[
1
]
Distance
It came to
perihelion
in 1971
[
4
]
and is currently 51.8
AU
from the Sun.
[
7
]
In April 2013, it moved beyond 50 AU from the Sun.
It has been observed 81 times over 10
oppositions
with
precovery
images back to 1974.
[
4
]
Physical characteristics
2005 QU
182
has a bright
absolute magnitude
of 3.74.
[
4
]
In 2012, the diameter of
2005 QU
182
was initially estimated to be
416
±
73 km
using data from the
Herschel Space Telescope
.
[
9
]
Later in 2020, the data was reanalyzed, which yielded a notably larger nominal diameter of
584
+155
−144
km
.
